data.body:
RCA (Phase 1, runtime-confirmed).

Mechanism: test_narrow_operation_persists_the_same_bytes_as_the_legacy_sequence (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_rich_reemit_state.py) builds two independent stores via _bound_store(), each calling BindingStore.bind_confirm -> BindingLifecycle.bind_confirm (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_lifecycle.py:151-166), which stamps created_at/updated_at from _now_iso() (second-granularity ...Z). Each _bound_store() makes exactly ONE clock read, at a separate wall-clock instant. When the two reads straddle a 1-second boundary the created_at/updated_at strings differ, so the two saved bindings.json files differ at byte index 72 (the created_at seconds digit) and the read_bytes()==read_bytes() assertion fails.

Runtime reproduction: injecting an advancing clock (43Z then 44Z) across the two bind_confirm calls reproduces the CI failure exactly -- 'At index 72 diff' (CI: 4 != 3; local legacy-vs-new: 3 vs 4 i.e. 51 vs 52). check_wall_clock_asserts did not catch this pattern (the timestamps are stamped in product code, asserted transitively via byte-equality).

Legitimacy: defect (flaky test). Product behavior is correct -- identical state + identical timestamp serializes to identical bytes. The non-determinism is purely the test's wall-clock dependency; no product/contract/schema change.

Fix (Phase 2, RED->GREEN): freeze binding_lifecycle._now_iso to a constant in the test before building the two stores, so both stamp identical timestamps. Defect-seeded mutation confirms the freeze is load-bearing: WITHOUT freeze + adversarial straddling clock -> bytes differ (RED); WITH freeze + same adversarial clock -> bytes identical (GREEN). Full file 36 passed; make lint (incl. wall-clock-asserts) clean; typecheck clean.
